turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I guess... they brought me in because of work. At the warehouse, I keep doing things... like, I'll just freeze with my arms up by the forklift. It's important to get the angles right. Did you know the forklift tires are made of solid rubber? They don't go flat. Anyway, I also copy the beeping sounds it makes, and the hand signals the drivers use. I have to. And I move the boxes in these strange little patterns. Even when everyone is yelling for me to stop, I can't. My uncle had a box collection once, mostly cigar boxes, stacked them up in his garage until the roof leaked... but yeah, they brought me here because of the warehouse stuff.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
turns.patient_response: Voices? No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Just the regular warehouse noises, really. Everyone hears the beeping and the metal clanking. Metal is so heavy, you know? A lot of people don't know that. Peanuts are legumes too. I'm not allergic, but this guy in my freshman dorm was so allergic he couldn't even be in the same room as a candy bar. He had one of those EpiPens. I heard those things are really expensive now, which doesn't seem fair if you just want to eat lunch... but no, no voices or anything.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any recent physical medical illnesses or head injuries?
turns.patient_response: Physical illness? No, I don't think so. I mean, my head is fine. No injuries. I did hit my elbow pretty hard on a pallet rack last month, though. Pallets are usually made of oak or southern yellow pine, did you know that? They have to be sturdy to hold all that weight. Wood is fascinating. Termites eat wood, but they don't actually digest it themselves. They have these little microorganisms in their guts that do it for them. It's like a tiny factory inside a bug. Factories are so loud. The warehouse is loud, but not like a real factory. My cousin worked in a car plant in Michigan, putting on doors. He said the smell of the paint would stick to his clothes for days. He had a blue uniform. Blue is a calming color, they say. They paint hospital walls blue sometimes. This room is kind of beige, though. Beige is a bit boring, don't you think? But yeah, no head injuries or anything like that. Just the elbow thing, and it healed up fine.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, wandering from pallets to termites, factories, and colors before finally returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt deeply depressed, down, or lost interest in things for weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response: Depressed? No, I don't... I don't think I've ever felt like that. I mean, I like doing things. I like the warehouse, even when they yell. Yelling is just... it's just sound waves, right? Sound waves traveling through the air. They bounce off the concrete floors. Concrete is actually a mixture of cement, water, and aggregates like sand or gravel. The Romans used concrete, you know. They built the Pantheon with it, and it's still standing. Thousands of years! Imagine building something that lasts that long. Most things today are just disposable. Like paper plates. We used paper plates at the company picnic last summer. They had barbecue. Barbecue sauce is mostly just ketchup and molasses, if you really look at the ingredients. Molasses is thick... kind of like how time feels when I'm freezing by the forklift. Just thick and slow. But no, I haven't been depressed or anything. I just have to do the patterns.
